answers:
1. I can't give you a call count per patient, I don't have that. What I do know is that confirmation calls were eating about 11 hours a week of front desk time, and honestly I think that's the bigger win here.

2. I'd rather not name the tool, our vendor contract doesn't let us name them in marketing without approval. What I can say is it's two-way texting, so patients can reschedule just by replying. I don't have the send timing handy.

3. I don't have a patient quote for this one. What I'd say is the reschedule-by-replying part is what actually moved the numbers, more than the reminders themselves.

4. The figure I have is those 11 hours a week saved on confirmation calls across the front desk. I don't have chairs-filled numbers, so I'd skip that.

5. The surprise was that it's the two-way part that mattered, not just sending reminders. Also, Joanna at our Gdańsk clinic noticed elderly patients would reply "OK" and still not show, so now we also phone every patient over 70. And Sopot only got to 12% and nobody's sure why. I'm a bit wary too that our six months included summer, when no-shows tend to drop anyway.
reply2:
I built this from your answers and kept your wording where I could. I left out the tool name, the send timing, and the chairs-filled figures, since you don't have or can't share them. The ending question is gone, and the closing line now says what you concluded.

<final>
We cut no-shows at Brightwell Dental Group from 18% to 7% in six months, across all 9 of our clinics.

We switched to two-way text messages, so patients can reschedule just by replying. Confirmation calls had been eating about 11 hours a week of front desk time, and I think that's the bigger win.

The surprise was that the two-way part mattered, not just sending reminders. Reschedule-by-replying is what actually moved the numbers.

It hasn't all worked. Joanna at our Gdańsk clinic noticed that elderly patients would reply "OK" and still not show, so now we also phone every patient over 70. Sopot only got to 12%, and nobody's sure why. I'm also a bit wary of the 7%, because our six months included summer, when no-shows tend to drop anyway.

If you run a multi-location practice and still rely on calls, it's worth testing.
</final>

It hasn't all worked. Joanna at our Gdańsk clinic noticed that elderly patients would reply "OK" and still not show, so now we also phone every patient over 70.
